t:
For payment to the Postal Service Fund for meeting the liabilities of the former Post Office Department to the Employees’ Compensation Fund pursuant to 39 U.S.C. 2004, $36,828,000.
This title may be cited as the “Postal Service Appropriations Act, 1996”.

fable.w: This section is a pure appropriation of funds to the Postal Service Fund plus a short-title clause. There is no tempting reading here: no outside party is consulted, no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is created. All actors and fund transfers are internal to the federal government.
fable.s: For payment to the Postal Service Fund for meeting the liabilities of the former Post Office Department to the Employees’ Compensation Fund pursuant to 39 U.S.C. 2004, $36,828,000.

opus.w: This is only an appropriation that moves money between federal funds to cover liabilities of the former Post Office Department, plus a short-title clause. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in any federal decision. Referring to federal funds and agencies is not participation, because every actor named is inside the federal government.
opus.s: For payment to the Postal Service Fund for meeting the liabilities of the former Post Office Department to the Employees’ Compensation Fund pursuant to 39 U.S.C. 2004, $36,828,000.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning:** Someone might see "Postal Service" and "Employees' Compensation Fund" and assume outside parties are involved. They aren't. This is a payment from one federal account to another plus a short-title clause. No outside party is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes an appropriation for the Postal Service to pay liabilities to an internal compensation fund. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The Postal Service and the Employees' Compensation Fund are federal entities, so this is an internal financial transaction.
qwen_chat.s: For payment to the Postal Service Fund for meeting the liabilities of the former Post Office Department to the Employees’ Compensation Fund pursuant to 39 U.S.C. 2004, $36,828,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Postal Service is an independent establishment, payments to it involve external entities. However, the Postal Service is a federal entity, and this section is merely an appropriation for internal liability settlement. There is no consultation, hearing, or coordination with non-federal parties (states, public, companies) required or described.
